junction.name: Polk Street & Eddy Street, San Francisco

claims.text: Polk Street & Eddy Street had 51 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $3.5 million a year.
6% of crashes here were recorded as “bicycle-parked car” crashes, against 0% at the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got continental crosswalks in 2019. Across the city: at 780 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+4%, 95% interval -25% to +33%) could be zero. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record.
The city's painted safety zones: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+2%, 95% interval -20% to +34%) could be zero); a second run of the same design on 780 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.5 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $524,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.8 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $272,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is responsible for Eddy Street, Polk Street, Willow Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is ready to draft from these facts.
